title: Tet
hook: the first tet in the Torah is in tov, good (Genesis 1:4)

segments.voice: Yesterday, glasses raised and one word: l'chaim, to life. Your line: chet for life. Today ends the week, with a letter the rabbis were glad to dream about.

Deep in the Talmud, in a tractate mostly about damages, oxen and pits and broken fences, the rabbis pause for something unexpected: dreams. What does it mean to dream about a certain animal, a certain fruit, a certain letter of the alef-bet? Some answers are puzzling. One is beautiful. If you see the letter tet in a dream, they say, it's a good sign. And they give a reason that sends you back to the first page of the Torah, to the very first morning of the world.
screen: `DREAMS, IN A BOOK OF DAMAGES.` → `A LETTER IN A DREAM.` → `TET IS A GOOD SIGN.`

segments.voice: First, the first morning. God says let there be light, and there is light. In the King James: "And God saw the light, that it was good." The Hebrew for good is tov, and it begins with tet. In the Talmud, in tractate Bava Kamma, that's the whole argument: the first time the Torah uses a tet, it's in the word good, so a tet in your dream is good news. Second, the rest of the chapter. Good doesn't appear once and vanish. As the world is made, light, sea, land, plants, stars, animals, the chapter keeps stopping to say God saw it was good. And at the end, looking at everything at once: "and, behold, it was very good." Tet comes back like a refrain. Third, the week just past. Seven letters, seven pictures. Gimel, running after someone in need. Dalet, a door, opened quietly. Heh, a breath added to a name. Vav, a hook that joins. Zayin, remembering on purpose. Chet, a toast to life. And now tet, good. Side by side, the alef-bet starts to read like a way of living. Fourth, your own week. The text pauses over the light and names it good before the rest of creation is finished. Good can be noticed on the first morning of anything.
screen: `AND GOD SAW THE LIGHT.` · `TOV: GOOD, BEGINNING WITH TET.` · `GOOD, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · `A WEEK OF LETTERS.` · then, large: `IT WAS GOOD.`

segments.voice: Look back over this week the way Genesis looks back over each day, and find one thing that was good: not perfect, good, like a meal, light through a window, a conversation that went better than expected. Hold it, say quietly to yourself, that was good, and if there's room, find one more; if you pray, give thanks for what you found.
Tet. The letter that begins tov, good, the word God says over the first light. Today's word.
Your line: tet for good. The rabbis even found it in dreams. Seven letters, one good week.

howItsDone: The first chapter of Genesis, with its refrain that God saw it was good, is read in synagogue at the start of each yearly cycle of Torah readings; some teachers of the alef-bet introduce tet with the word tov.
